title: Bicycle shop repair handoff
brief:
Complete the following real project in the current, initially empty directory. Choose the deliverables, media, tools, structure and implementation that serve the intended user. Build usable artifacts and check your work. Deliver the project itself. Omit personally identifying credits, author signatures and model or toolchain identity labels. No network access or credentials are provided.

Build a visual and editorial kit for a bicycle shop's repair pickup counter. Customers often arrive during the evening rush, and both they and the cashier need to see what work was done, what they paid for, and whom to ask about a follow-up. Create an example customer handoff using this fictional job: rear tube $9, rear flat repair $18, and chain cleaning $12. The shop takes questions in person on weekdays from 4 to 6 p.m. Choose artifacts for the counter and for customers to keep. The counter has a single upright display holder and little spare surface space.

files.body:
# Spoke House repair pickup kit

## Set up the counter

Print the [counter sign](print/counter-sign.pdf) single-sided at actual size on portrait US Letter paper (8.5 × 11 inches). Place it in the upright holder facing the queue. The sign shows an example so customers can see how parts and labor appear on their own record.

Print the [completed customer slips](print/customer-slip.pdf) for the example job or the [blank slips](print/blank-slip.pdf) for other jobs. Use the same paper and settings. Cut once across the dotted center line to make two half-letter slips. Keep the stack at the register behind the counter.

## At pickup

On a blank slip, enter each part or service on its own line, mark it as part or labor, and enter the charge. Confirm payment before filling in “Total paid.” Hand the customer their copy and use the slip to walk through the work.

For the example job, the cashier can say:

> We replaced your rear tube and cleaned your chain. The tube was $9, the flat repair was $18, and the chain cleaning was $12. You paid $39. Here’s your copy. If you have questions, ask the repair cashier here on weekdays from 4 to 6 p.m.

The [editable artwork](artwork/) contains one SVG for each print sheet. Keep both copies on a slip sheet in sync when editing.

# Bicycle repair pickup kit

Print on US Letter (8½ × 11 in) at **Actual size / 100%**. Cut along the corner marks. The sign is sized for a **5 × 7 in portrait holder**. Keep the cut slips with the repair tickets or at the register.

At pickup, match the customer to their repair ticket. Review each part or service and its charge, confirm the amount paid, and hand over the slip with the receipt. For future jobs, fill in the job number, date, completed work, charges, and total paid.

**Sample handoff**

> We replaced the rear tube. The tube was $9 and the rear flat repair was $18. We also cleaned the chain for $12. You paid $39 total. If you have questions, stop by on a weekday between 4 and 6 p.m. and ask for the repair team.
